title: Conservation of Energy
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Conservation of Energy from GCSE Physics.
meta_desc: GCSE Physics adventure on energy stores, transfers and conservation.
final_note: You walked through stores, transfers and conservation.

concepts.def: Energy cannot be created or destroyed

walkthroughs.body_html:
Stores include kinetic, gravitational, elastic, chemical, thermal, nuclear.

Transfers: mechanical work, electrical, heating, radiation.

Total energy is conserved.

Some is usually wasted as heat or sound.

Efficiency = useful / total.

Improve by reducing friction or insulation.

mcqs.q: When energy is 'lost' as heat due to friction, what has really happened?
options: Energy has been transferred to the thermal store of the surroundings — it's not destroyed, just dissipated.
Energy has been used up and no longer exists.
Energy has been converted into mass following E=mc^2.
Kinetic energy stays the same because mass hasn't changed.

mcqs.q: Can a device ever be 100 percent efficient?
options: Energy has been converted into mass following E=mc^2.
Efficiency above 100 percent is possible if the device extracts ambient energy.
A well-designed device can be 100 percent efficient by eliminating all friction.
In practice, no — some energy is always transferred to less useful stores (e.g. heat to surroundings).

mcqs.q: If a car doubles its speed, what happens to its kinetic energy?
options: Efficiency above 100 percent is possible if the device extracts ambient energy.
It quadruples (because KE = 1/2 mv^2 — kinetic energy is proportional to v^2).
Kinetic energy doubles because energy is proportional to speed.
Kinetic energy stays the same because mass hasn't changed.
